name: Vapi
summary: Vapi provides an API-native platform for businesses to build, deploy, and manage voice AI agents at scale.
overview: Vapi is a voice-AI infrastructure provider that lets enterprises configure and operate voice agents. It announced a $50 million Series B in May 2026 after reporting one billion calls; reporting placed the post-money valuation at roughly $500 million.

facts.label: Latest financing
facts.note: Vapi raised $50 million in Series B funding at an approximately $500 million valuation.

bull_case: A developer-centric platform can benefit as enterprises move voice agents from pilots to high-volume customer interactions.
bear_case: Voice-AI quality, regulatory compliance, and competition from cloud and contact-centre platforms can constrain long-term margins.
latest_round: May 2026 Series B: $50M at an approximately $500M valuation
directory_notes: Public financing and operating data remain limited.

intelligence.description: API-native voice-AI infrastructure for building and operating enterprise voice agents.
company: Vapi provides an API-native platform for building, deploying, and managing voice agents. The company says customers including Amazon, New York Life, and Intuit use its platform for voice-AI applications at scale.

In May 2026, Vapi announced a $50 million Series B led by Peak XV and said it had reached one billion calls. The company did not announce a valuation; TechCrunch reported a valuation of around $500 million after the financing.
intelligence.why_it_matters: Voice is a costly and operationally sensitive customer-service channel, making it a consequential deployment area for AI agents. Vapi's funding and customer claims offer a private-market signal on adoption beyond text-based assistants.

changed.text: Vapi announced a $50M Series B; reporting placed the valuation at about $500M.

takeaways: The May 2026 Series B brought total funding to $72M, according to Vapi.
High-volume enterprise voice deployments are the core demand signal.
The profile treats the $500M valuation as reported rather than company-disclosed.
